THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MAY 1, 1937

Puppet State,
German Envoy
Face Difficulty

Opinions Differ Widely
On Trade Matters As
Parleys Begun

KNOLL IN CHARGE
ON REICH SIDE

Germans Seek Change
In Previous Pact,
Puppets Opposed

TOKYO, April 27.—(Reuters).—
Germany's trade representative, Dr.
Karl Knoll, who recently arrived in
Changchun as the head of the new
German Trade Mission, will be in
charge of Germany's delegation to
negotiate a renewal of the Nazi
trade agreement with "Manchukuo,"
which expires on May 31.
Dr. Knoll played an important
part in the conclusion of the pre-
sent agreement. He was a member
of the German Economic Mission
to Japan and "Manchukuo" in 1936,
of which Dr. Otto C. Kiep was head.
Before opening the negotiations,
Dr. Knoll will obtain the opinions
of the German consular authorities
in Mukden, Harbin and other Man-
churian cities and of German
traders in Manchuria. He will also
visit Tokyo to consult the German
Embassy.
Although observers are confident
an amicable settlement will be
reached in the German-"Manchu-
kuo" trade parley, the delegates
are expected to enter the conference
with strongly divergent opinions on
several points.
To Insist On Revision
German merchants are expected
to insist upon revision of the pre-
sent agreement to provide for
simplification of procedures, a more
favorable trade ration, a curb on
the re-export of German products
to North China, and a better posi-
tion for meeting the competition of
other countries.
The "Manchukuo" Government
has decided to reject any proposal
for revision of the agreement to
make it applicable to German im-
ports of "Manchukuo" goods via
Japan or any other third country,
it is authoritatively stated in
Changchun. The decision was made
after Mr. Hikichi Kato, head of the
"Manchukuo" trade representation
in Berlin, asked for full instructions
on the subject.
Mr. Kato filed his request, it is
believed, in anticipation of the
possibility that the question will
become an important issue in the
negotiations.
Official circles in Changchun
maintain that the agreement, both
in spirit and in letter, is one con-
cluded between "Manchukuo" and
Germany as independent States.
Operation of the present agree-
ment has proved rather unsatisfac-
tory, according to current reports.
German traders in Manchuria con-
tend that the pact is loaded with
troublesome procedure and is not
practical, and hold that they are
restricted in their activities by
Germany's vigorous exchange con-
trol measures.
Placed At Disadvantage
They have thus been placed, they
contend, in a disadvantageous
position, and their predicament has
been made more serious by the
concerted competition of British,
American and French traders. If
the situation is not corrected, Ger-
man traders in "Manchukuo" fear
that their business will be seriously
affected.
Desiring to protect the interests
of German merchants in Man-
churia, the German Government is
expected to propose a fundamental
revision of the agreement, intro-
ducing a radical change in the
present ratios of the barter system,
which is based on importation of
Y.25,000,000 worth of German pro-
ducts into Manchuria and Y.100,-
000,000 worth of Manchurian pro-
ducts into Germany.
The German consular authorities
and traders in Manchuria are
understood to hope for revision of
the agreement on the following
lines:
1. Procedures required by the
agreement should be simplified,
thereby preventing possible losses
as a result of delays.
2. The present barter ration of
one for Germany to four for "Man-
chukuo" should be revised in favor
of Germany to relieve the depressed
status of German traders in Man-
churia.
3. When the agreement was
signed last year, the German de-
legation was of the opinion that
"Manchukuo" and the Kwantung
Leased Territory could easily con-
sume Y.25,000,000 worth of German
products annually. This expectation
has not materialized, since part of
the German products imported into
Manchuria have been re-exported
into North China.
German Traders Hit
This re-exportation, combined
with Japan's economic advance in
North China, has seriously inter-
fered with German interests in
that part of China, and the in-
terests of German traders in Man-
churia have been affected unfavor-
ably. The German interests con-
sider they should receive more
favorable treatment.
4. British, American and French
competition has been severe since
the agreement was signed. British
dumping has checked the penetra-
tion of German products into Man-
churia. The German delegation
seeks to turn the tide in its own
favor.
Despite the apparent bases for
possible disagreement, observers feel
that the prevailing friendship be-
tween Japan and Germany will be
a factor in smoothing out the dif-
ficulties, especially in view of the
recent visit to Germany of Mr.
Chuichi Chashi, Foreign Vice-Minis-
ter of "Manchukuo."

伪政权、
德国公使
面临困难

谈判开始之际
贸易问题上的
意见大相径庭

诺尔负责
德方事务

德国人寻求改变
先前协定，
伪政权表示反对

东京，4月27日.—(路透社).—
德国贸易代表卡尔·诺尔博士 (Dr. Karl Knoll) 最近抵达长春，担任新成立的德国贸易代表团团长，他将负责德国代表团与“满洲国”就续签将于5月31日到期的纳粹贸易协定进行的谈判。
诺尔博士在达成现行协定方面发挥了重要作用。他是1936年德国赴日本和“满洲国”经济代表团的成员，该团由奥托·C·基普博士 (Dr. Otto C. Kiep) 率领。
在开启谈判之前，诺尔博士将征询德国驻沈阳、哈尔滨及其他满洲城市领事当局以及德国在满洲商人的意见。他还将访问东京，与德国大使馆磋商。
尽管观察家们确信德“满”贸易谈判会达成友好解决方案，但预计代表们在几个问题上将带着严重分歧的意见进入会议。
坚持修订
预计德国商人将坚持修订现行协定，以简化程序、提供更有利的贸易比例、遏制德国产品向华北的再出口，并在应对其他国家竞争时处于更有利的地位。
据长春方面的权威消息，“满洲国”政府已决定拒绝任何旨在使协定适用于德国经由日本或任何第三国进口“满洲国”货物的修订提议。这一决定是在“满洲国”驻柏林贸易代表处处长加藤彦吉先生 (Mr. Hikichi Kato) 请求就此事项给予全面指示后作出的。
据信，加藤先生提出请求是预见到该问题可能成为谈判中的一个重要议题。
长春官方人士坚持认为，无论从精神还是条文上看，该协定都是“满洲国”与德国作为独立国家之间缔结的。
据目前报道，现行协定的运作结果相当令人不满。在满洲的德国商人声称，该协定充满了繁琐的程序且不切实际，并认为他们的活动受到德国严厉外汇管制措施的限制。
处于不利地位
他们声称，因此他们处于不利地位，而英国、美国和法国商人的联合竞争使他们的困境更加严峻。如果不纠正这种局面，在“满洲国”的德国商人担心他们的生意将受到严重影响。
为了保护德国在满洲商人的利益，预计德国政府将提议对协定进行根本性修订，对现行易货制度的比例进行激进调整，该制度基于向满洲进口价值2,500万日元 (Y.25,000,000) 的德国产品和向德国进口价值1亿日元 (Y.100,000,000) 的满洲产品。
据悉，德国驻满洲领事当局和商人希望按以下方针修订协定：
1. 应简化协定所需的程序，从而防止因延误而可能造成的损失。
2. 应将目前德国为一、“满洲国”为四的易货比例修订为有利于德国，以缓解在满洲的德国商人的萧条状况。
3. 去年签署协定时，德国代表团认为“满洲国”和关东租借地每年可以轻松消耗价值2,500万日元的德国产品。这一预期并未实现，因为部分进口到满洲的德国产品已被再出口到华北。
打击德国商人
这种再出口，加上日本在华北的经济扩张，严重干扰了德国在该地区的利益，并对在满洲的德国商人的利益产生了不利影响。德国利益相关者认为他们应该得到更优惠的待遇。
4. 自协定签署以来，英国、美国和法国的竞争一直非常激烈。英国的倾销阻碍了德国产品进入满洲。德国代表团试图扭转局势，使其有利于己方。
尽管存在可能导致分歧的明显依据，但观察家们认为，日本和德国之间普遍的友谊将成为化解困难的一个因素，特别是鉴于“满洲国”外交次长查士琦先生 (Mr. Chuichi Chashi) 最近访问了德国。

Dr. Karl Knoll, a member of the German Mission which last year visited the Orient, will return to Manchoukuo soon to conduct negotiations for the revision and renewal of the commercial treaty between the Reich and the new Empire, concluded last April and expiring this June. The negotiations, political observers in Tokyo believe, will be influenced by the Japanese-German anti-Comintern pact. The German-Manchuria agreement, which provided for the barter of the new Empire's stables, mainly soya beans, for the Reich's machinery, has drawn strong criticism from the business interests in Manchuria who regard it as unfavourable to the new State. Of 7,993 tons of soya beans imported by Germany during last November, only 986 tons came from Manchuria, according to figures revealed by the Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha. CHINA DEVELOPMENT
EULOGIZED

Dr. O. Kiep on Far East in
World Economy

PLENTY OF ROOM FOR
CO-OPERATION

Berlin, Nov. 8.
Before the German World Economic Society, Dr. Otto Kiep, leader of the German Economic Commission for the Far East, to-day spoke on "World Economic Impressions from the Far East."

Dr. Kiep pointed out that, in recent years, the Far East had greatly increased in importance for world economy. This was partly due to the rapid development undergone by certain national economic territories of the Far East and partly to the efforts made by European countries to open new markets for their products and find new sources of indispensable raw materials.

German exports, in particular, had met with success in the Far East in applying the principles of Dr. Hjalmar Schacht's New Plan, namely, that Germany could only buy from foreign countries as much as she could pay for and would purchase her raw materials from countries which bought industrial products from her, and Germany had a keen interest in developing these relations further.

Dr. Kiep stated that, above all, the development of economic affairs in China had been an active one. In pursuance of Dr. Sun Yat-sen's principles, the National Government in China, simultaneously with the work of pacification and reconstruction of Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, had taken the programme of economic development vigorously in hand.

Room for Co-operation

In consequence, the producing and consuming power of the Chinese people had already risen noticeably and, if continued, would become an increasingly important factor in world economy. The plans, already partially realized—for the development of communications and national industries, closely connected with far-reaching plans to overcome the danger of floods and famine—formed an immense programme of world economic measures, offering room for the co-operation of foreign industries, especially for those who were prepared to buy increasing quantities of Chinese raw materials.

In Siam, under the new national leadership, economic development is beginning to follow quite different lines and to experience a stimulation similar to that in China, while, in the remaining territories of the East Asiatic region, an increase of both production and consumption is noticeable all round.

The significance of the Far East for world economy, Dr. Kiep continued, is revealed by the fact that almost half of the world's population lives there and has a considerably greater natural increase than either Europe or America. The economic inter-dependence of Asia and Europe is indicated by the fact that one-sixth of the total European imports comes from the Far East and about one-quarter of its export is being shipped to there.

Every increase of the movement of merchandise between the two regions must result in a corresponding stimulation and fertilization of the economy between both parts.—Trans. China News Min.

赞颂中国
发展

基普博士论远东在
世界经济中的地位

合作空间广阔

柏林，11月8日。
今天，德国远东经济委员会主席奥托·基普博士 (Dr. Otto Kiep) 在德国世界经济学会面前发表了题为“来自远东的世界经济印象”的演讲。

基普博士指出，近年来，远东在世界经济中的重要性大大增加。这部分是由于远东某些国民经济区域的快速发展，部分是由于欧洲国家努力为其产品开辟新市场并寻找不可或缺的新原材料来源。

特别是德国出口，在应用沙赫特博士 (Dr. Hjalmar Schacht) 的新计划原则方面，在远东取得了成功，即德国只能购买其有能力支付的外国商品，并从购买其工业产品的国家采购原材料，德国对进一步发展这些关系有着浓厚的兴趣。

基普博士表示，最重要的是，中国的经济事务发展一直非常活跃。遵循孙中山先生的原则，中国政府在蒋介石将军进行绥靖和重建工作的同时， vigorously 着手实施经济发展计划。

合作空间

因此，中国人民的生产和消费能力已经显著上升，如果持续下去，将成为世界经济中越来越重要的因素。已经部分实现的交通和民族工业发展计划，与克服水患和饥荒危险的深远计划紧密相连，构成了一个庞大的世界经济措施方案，为外国工业的合作提供了空间，特别是对于那些愿意购买越来越多中国原材料的企业。

在暹罗，在新的国家领导下，经济发展开始走上截然不同的道路，并经历了类似于中国的刺激，而在东亚地区的其他领土，生产和消费均有普遍增长。

基普博士继续说道，远东对世界经济的重要性体现在这样一个事实：世界近一半的人口居住在那里，其自然增长率远高于欧洲或美洲。亚洲和欧洲的经济相互依赖性体现在这样一个事实：欧洲总进口量的六分之一来自远东，而其出口量的约四分之一运往那里。

两个地区之间商品流通的每一增加，必然导致双方经济的相应刺激和繁荣。—译自《中国新闻简报》

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, MAY 18, 1936
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL S. D. REGS. J. B. D. 47240）

Meaning Of German-
"Manchukuo" Agreement

The German-"Manchukuo" trade agreement was "engineered" by Japan, declares the Shun Pao, and therefore it must be of some political significance. The new agreement, it believes, furnishes partial proof of the existence of the alleged German-Japanese military pact of mutual assistance. It continues:

The trade agreement between Germany and "Manchukuo," signed by Dr. Otto Kiep, head of the German Economic Mission to the Far East, will assist the Reich in balancing Germany's foreign trade, but we believe that the agreement has political as well as economic significance. Coming at the same time as the reports of a German-Japanese military pact of mutual assistance, we cannot ignore its possible results.

There can be no doubt that the trade agreement was engineered by Japan, because Japan, in strengthening her foothold in the Far East, is eager to gain the friendship of Germany and she is willing to let Germany share some of the profits from trade in the Three Eastern Provinces.

Germany is facing financial difficulties at home because of the wall built around her by the Little Entente and she must therefore seek raw materials abroad, particularly in the Orient. Germany is willing to overlook Japanese activities in China in order to gain Japanese support in securing supplies in "Manchukuo."

It is evident that the German-"Manchukuo" trade agreement is a link in German-Japanese relations. One cannot but believe the rumor that the conclusion of this agreement means that a pact of mutual assistance between the two countries is also in existence.

德“满”协定的
含义

《申报》宣称，德“满”贸易协定是由日本“策划”的，因此它一定具有某种政治意义。该报认为，新协定为所谓德日军事互助协定存在的说法提供了部分证据。该报继续写道：

由德国赴远东经济代表团团长奥托·基普博士 (Dr. Otto Kiep) 签署的德“满”贸易协定，将有助于帝国平衡德国的对外贸易，但我们认为该协定具有政治和经济双重意义。鉴于有关德日军事互助协定的报道同时出现，我们不能忽视其可能的后果。

毫无疑问，该贸易协定是由日本策划的，因为日本在巩固其在远东的立足点时，渴望获得德国的友谊，并愿意让德国分享东北三省贸易的一些利润。

由于小协约国 (Little Entente) 筑起的围墙，德国在国内面临财政困难，因此必须在海外，特别是在东方寻求原材料。为了获得日本在确保“满洲国”供应方面的支持，德国愿意对日本在华活动视而不见。

显然，德“满”贸易协定是德日关系中的一个环节。人们不得不相信这样的谣言，即该协定的缔结意味着两国之间也存在互助协定。

SHANGHAI SPECIAL DISTRICT KUOMINTANG TO HOLD MEETING TO COMMEMORATE THE MAY 9 ANNIVERSARY

May 9 being an anniversary of national humiliation, the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang has decided to convene a general memorial meeting of representatives of various local public bodies at its office at 10 a.m. that day. The public has also been notified to hoist the national flags at half mast as a means to commemorate the occasion.

Shun Pao published the following editorial on May 6 :-

THE INNER MOTIVE OF THE CONCLUSION OF THE GERMAN-MANCHUKUO COMMERCIAL TREATY

Ever since the arrival in Japan last winter of the Far Eastern Economic Inspection Group under the leadership of Dr. Otto C. Kiep, the members of the Group immediately set forth to negotiate with the Japanese government officials regarding measures for a commercial co-operation between Germany, Japan and "Manchukuo". From the recent telegraphic reports, it is learned that the Group, representing Germany, has concluded a Commercial Treaty with "Manchukuo" at Tokyo on April 30, whereby it is stipulated that Germany has to pay 75% in foreign rates and 25% in Mark notes of the price of all materials, such as soya beans, wool, etc., exported to Germany from "Manchukuo", while the importations to "Manchukuo" from Germany should not exceed the limit of the exports to Germany from "Manchukuo".

That the conclusion of this treaty is due to the initiative of "the certain nation" is obvious and without doubt. With the intention of advancing and expanding its influence in the Far East, this ambitious nation has therefore anxiously desired to secure Germany's assistance, even willing to allow the latter to share its benefits in the Three Eastern Provinces, because it is always beneficial for this nation to exchange the soya beans which are abundant in the Three Eastern Provinces for aeroplanes and guns from Germany.

It has long been rumoured that a military pact has been concluded between Germany and Japan. The conclusion of this commercial treaty between Germany and "Manchukuo" has further corroborated that it is not merely a fabrication that a military pact has been concluded between Germany and Japan.

Dr. Kiep Defends
Regime Of Hitler

Says Economic Verdict
Clearly In Favor Of
Present Authority

"If economic conditions are taken as a measure for the success or failure of National Socialism in Germany, the verdict must undoubtedly turn in favor of the Hitler regime," began Minister Dr. Otto C. Kiep, head of the German Economic Mission to the Far East, as he opened his address before the Pan-Pacific Association in the Metropole Hotel this afternoon.

Luncheon was served to about 120 persons before the address, which was on "Economic Conditions in Germany," nearly half a hundred the audience being members of the German community, which has been entertaining Dr. and Mrs. Kiep since their arrival here on Monday from the South.

Dr. Wang Presides
Dr. C. T. Wang presided at the gathering and introduced the speaker; Mr. R. C. W. Behrend, German Consul in Shanghai, Mr. E. von Randow, of the Consulate, Mr. S. R. von Winterfeldt, the new German Commercial Attache, and Mr. P. T. Chen, representing Dr. H. H. Kung, president of the Association, were among the honor guests.

Others present included: Mr. and Mrs. T. Huldermann, Dr. Kempe, Mr. Rudolph Laurenz, Mr. and Mrs. Feuerholzer, Mr. H. Steeneck, Captain Fusewind, Mr. P. von Schubert, Mr. W. Balthaser, Mr. S. Lahrnann, Mr. G. T. Siemssen, Mr. R. S. Rudloff, Mr. K. Schaefer, Dr. J. Uang Ly, Mrs. Earl H. Cressey, Mr. and Mrs. C. C. Newson, Mr. and Mrs. Chester Fritz, Mr. H. A. Scott, Mr. Bruce Macdonald, Dr. D. Engel, Mr. M. T. Chou, Baroness Ungern Sternberg, and many others.

Outstanding Results
Dr. Kiep said in part:
"Even the most adverse critics of Germany have not questioned the outstanding results of the German recovery program and the vast improvement of economic conditions since the advent of the Hitler Government. The net outcome so far has been a reduction of the number of unemployed from 6½ to less than 2 millions and an increase of the volume of economic activity in all spheres to an extent and at a pace unsurpassed, if not unequalled, in any other country.

"These and other favorable developments in the domain of public finances, banking conditions, trade revival, social welfare etc. in Germany bear testimony to the fact that it is possible, even for countries lacking financial reserves or resources, to overcome the effects of the great crisis if the people can be united and the Government endowed with authority to enforce necessary measure.

Severe Strain
"Again taking economic conditions as measure, it can safely be stated that no country, at least no large and densely peopled country, industrially organized and with a socially and educationally advanced population, has been subjected to such severe strain and pressure as Germany was through the world war and the postwar politics of the victors.

"It is necessary in order to understand Germany of today, to recall the fact that the German people were actually starved out during the war, that the blockade was continued for a year after the cessation of hostilities and that from 1919 until 1932 European politics were, as far as Germany was concerned, restricted to the problem of political and economic subjugation of that country to the benefit of its chief wartime opponents for as long a period as possible.

"The result was in the political sphere a status of inferior right and political inequality in the society of nations with corresponding reactions of the psychology of the German people and in the economic sphere a debt burden of about 30 billion Goldmarks.

Huge Foreign Debt
"This huge foreign debt has been the cause and measure of economic conditions in Germany since the outbreak of the crisis in 1931. The recall of the foreign loans brought about the collapse of the economic, social and political structure of the country, which in its further development necessitated the organisation of the new state under Adolf Hitler. The repayment of the loans, still continuing today, is responsible for the enormous strain on German finances witnessed during the last years and for the reduction of the standard of living of the people.

"It is surprising to see features of the latter, as the recent scarcity of butter and fats in Germany, being registered with satisfaction in certain organs of the international press as a sign of weakness of German economy under the new regime, instead of realizing the extent of sacrifice brought by the German people to repay their foreign debts and of voicing disapproval on a return of wartime happenings 18 years after peace had been proclaimed. The burden of foreign debt still remaining and calling for repayment is the cause of Germany's reduced purchasing power in the world market and, here again, it is surprising to find governments and business interests complaining about the German import restrictions under the New Plan in the very countries which are responsible for these restrictions by their reparation policies. They are the same circles, who in the past used to justify their reparation demands by insisting that if the German people would work more and live on less they could well pay for all costs of the world war.

Trade With China
"In spite of these import restrictions it has been possible to assure the necessary importation of raw materials into Germany to keep German industry at work and to enable the National Recovery Programme to be carried through, although a considerable reorganisation of Germany's foreign trade had to be effected under the New Plan.

"Under his system Germany's purchases from China, which offers a favorable market to Germany, have according to the figures recently published by the Chinese Institute of Social and Economic Research, increased from 1934-35 by 45% and there is all reason to believe that this tendency will continue. Assuming that the production of raw materials in the various countries of the world will continue to expand as heretofore and taking it for granted, which we may, that German industry will always be able to produce sufficient for exportation to pay her raw material requirements, the main condition precedent to a satisfactory working of German economy can be considered as established."

Uang Ly 博士、Earl H. Cressey 夫人、C. C. Newson 夫妇、Chester Fritz 夫妇、H. A. Scott 先生、Bruce Macdonald 先生、D. Engel 博士、M. T. Chou 先生、Ungern Sternberg 男爵夫人等许多人。

显著成果
基普博士部分发言如下：
“即使是德国最严厉的批评者，也未质疑德国复兴计划的显著成果，以及自希特勒政府上台以来经济状况的巨大改善。迄今为止的最终结果是，失业人数从650万减少到不足200万，各领域的经济活动量以其他国家望尘莫及（即便不是无与伦比）的程度和速度增长。

“德国在公共财政、银行状况、贸易复苏、社会福利等领域的这些及其他有利发展，证明了一个事实：即使对于缺乏金融储备或资源的国家，只要人民能够团结，且政府拥有执行必要措施的权威，就有可能克服大危机的影响。

严峻压力
“再次以经济状况为衡量标准，可以稳妥地断言，没有任何一个国家——至少没有一个工业组织化、人口社会和教育程度较高的大型人口稠密国家——像德国那样，因世界大战及战后战胜国的政治而遭受如此严峻的紧张和压力。

“要理解今日的德国，有必要回顾这样一个事实：德国人民在战争期间实际上处于饥饿状态；停战后封锁又持续了一年；而且从1919年到1932年，就德国而言，欧洲政治局限于将该国在政治上和经济上屈从于其主要战时对手的问题，且这种状态被尽可能长久地维持。

“其结果是在政治领域，在国际社会中处于权利低下和政治不平等的地位，并引起德国人民心理的相应反应；在经济领域，则背负了约300亿金马克的债务负担。

巨额外债
“自1931年危机爆发以来，这笔巨额外债一直是德国经济状况的原因和衡量标准。外国贷款的召回导致了该国经济、社会和政治结构的崩溃，这在其后续发展中使得在阿道夫·希特勒领导下组织新国家成为必要。至今仍在继续的贷款偿还，是近年来德国财政承受巨大压力的原因，也是人民生活水平下降的原因。

“令人惊讶的是，诸如近期德国黄油和脂肪短缺等现象，竟被国际新闻界的某些机构满意地记录为新政权下德国经济疲软的标志，而不是认识到德国人民为偿还外债所做出的牺牲程度，也不是对和平宣告18年后重现战时情景表示不满。剩余且需偿还的外债负担是德国在世界市场上购买力下降的原因，在此方面，同样令人惊讶的是，那些因其赔款政策而导致这些限制的国家中的政府和商业利益集团，竟然抱怨‘新计划’下的德国进口限制。正是这些圈子，过去曾坚持认为，如果德国人民更加努力工作并降低生活消费，他们就能支付世界大战的所有费用，以此为其赔款要求辩护。

对华贸易
“尽管存在这些进口限制，但仍有可能确保德国必要的原材料进口，以维持德国工业运转并使国家复兴计划得以实施，尽管在‘新计划’下不得不对外贸进行相当程度的重组。

“在这一体系下，根据中国社会经济研究所最近公布的数据，德国从提供有利市场的中国的采购额在1934-35年间增加了45%，且有充分理由相信这一趋势将持续下去。假设世界各国原材料的生产将继续像以往一样扩张，并且理所当然地认为（我们可以这样认为）德国工业将始终能够生产足够的出口产品以支付其原材料需求，那么德国经济满意运作的主要先决条件可被视为已确立。”

The German Economic Mission To The Far East

THE German Economic Mission to the Far East has at last arrived at this premier port of China, after its visit to various Japanese and Manchurian trade centers and North China. The route the mission takes has caused much speculation and indeed it has been suggested from many sources that the object the mission has on hand is to conclude certain gigantic deals with certain “foreign” traders in Manchuria, especially for the purchase of beans. However that may be, the mission was well received in this city by the Institute of International Relations. At the reception, Dr. O. C. Kiep, head of the mission, delivered an illuminating speech on Sino-German trade relations.

Dr. Kiep was greatly admired by his audience for his simple, direct, and candid manner of expression. The shrinkage of international trade through customs barriers, quotas, exchange control, and other restrictions, he regarded as one of the most vital phenomena in the present world-wide economic crisis. But the real root of the evil he traced to the reduced purchasing power brought about through the losses of the World War and the enormous amount of debt it left behind. Germany has to bear the brunt of all this in the form of crushing indemnities, in addition to the loss of her former colonies and foreign markets. But Germany, under the leadership of the Reichsfuehrer, is fighting to deliver herself from the grip of such economic crisis. Dr. Schacht, Minister of Economics, has formulated the New Plan to reorganize Germany’s foreign trade. Its aim is, according to Dr. Kiep; “to rationalize and co-ordinate German imports and exports and to prevent a new debt arising from an excess of the former.” At this point, Dr. Kiep was apologetic and admitted:

This planned economy has entailed many undesirable impediments to the transaction of commercial business to and from Germany. But a certain amount of governmental interference is unavoidable in every planned economy and the German Government seeks as much as possible to adjust the measures taken to the requirements and the trade conditions of the different countries with which Germany is engaged in trade.

The actual working of the plan, the head of the German Economic Mission described it in the following terms:

Under the New Plan the structure of Germany’s foreign trade, has been subjected to considerable changes, mainly on the import side. Imports have had to be restricted to indispensable food-stuffs and to the raw materials essential for the upkeep of German industry. At the same time the lack of foreign exchange has reduced German imports from those countries in which purchasing power arising from German exports is not sufficiently available and has increased German purchases of raw materials in countries which can offer a market for Germany has no oversea possessions from which her requirements in raw materials can be derived. She therefore seeks to develop her trade relations with countries which produce raw materials and have need for industrial importation.

Under such an arrangement China has much to gain. Raw materials she has aplenty, and she can very well dispose of them on the German market. Of finished products, though she is now able to meet her own needs in part, she still stands in increasing need. When properly developed, China may offer an excellent market not only to Germany but to other leading industrial countries as well. Dr. Keip observed:

It is particularly noteworthy that Germany’s imports from China have been increasing at a greater rate than her exports to China during this period in spite of the fact that the total of German imports had to be reduced under the New Plan.

Unfortunately the head of the German Economic Mission failed to be entirely direct and candid and inform us whether “Germany’s imports from China” included imports from Manchuria now under the forceful occupation of another Power. In view of the belief prevalent among a certain section of the Chinese people, already mentioned, this omission is particularly unfortunate; for under the present situation, to quote one of our morning contemporaries, “it would not be difficult to appreciate the grave concern with which the Chinese people may look upon any development likely to embarrass their endeavor toward redress through means both economic and political.”

The international outlook for the moment is somewhat distressing in the light of constant rumors of strife in one part or another of this distressed world. In a joint universal endeavor to avert further intensification of an already intense war-like atmosphere, Germany, in her own interest, should play an important and useful role. On the manner in which she may proceed to tackle her diplomatic issues in Europe and in the Orient will depend, to a large extent, peace among nations and as a consequence the maintenance of the existing markets for her products and the sources to which she must periodically look for the supply of raw materials. Economic interests are frankly at the root of all wars, and economics and politics can never be divorced one from the other.

It is hoped that that Dr. Kiep will, when opportunity offers itself, inform the Chinese public of the fundamental trade policy of his country, including issues of a quasi-political nature. For, all told, politics have something to do with trade. Indeed, the phenomenal gain of German trade in China since the World War may be attributed in part to their loss of extraterritoriality. Other things being equal, a Chinese business man would naturally prefer to place his orders with the firm not enjoying extraterritorial rights, because should trouble arise out of the deal, he would not be placed under the difficulty of settling the case in a consular court. If the German Trade Mission made its trade policy sufficiently clear and satisfactory from the Chinese point of view, then, as Dr. Kiep rightly pointed out:

With the further development of the natural resources of China, to which end the present National Government is so successfully devoting interest and energies, Germany can satisfy her requirements of raw material and mineral ores in a growing measure on the Chinese market.

And we may add that China can satisfy her need of manufactured articles in a growing measure from German sources, too.

德国赴远东经济代表团

德国赴远东经济代表团在访问了日本和满洲各地的贸易中心以及华北之后，终于抵达了中国这个首要港口。该代表团的行程路线引发了诸多猜测，确实有许多消息来源暗示，该代表团此行的目的是与满洲的某些“外国”商人达成某些巨额交易，特别是购买大豆。无论如何，该代表团在本市受到了国际关系学会的热情接待。在招待会上，代表团团长奥·C·基普（O. C. Kiep）博士就中德贸易关系发表了富有启发性的演讲。

基普博士以其简单、直接和坦率的表达方式赢得了听众的高度赞赏。他认为，通过关税壁垒、配额、外汇管制和其他限制导致国际贸易萎缩，是当前世界性经济危机中最重要的现象之一。但他将祸根追溯至第一次世界大战造成的损失及其留下的巨额债务所导致的购买力下降。除了失去前殖民地和海外市场外，德国还以沉重的赔款形式承担了这一切的主要负担。但是，在帝国元首的领导下，德国正在努力摆脱这种经济危机的束缚。经济部长沙赫特（Schacht）博士制定了重组德国外贸的“新计划”。据基普博士称，其目标是：“使德国的进出口合理化和协调化，并防止因进口过多而产生新的债务。”在此处，基普博士表示歉意并承认：

这种计划经济给往返德国的商业交易带来了许多不良阻碍。但在任何计划经济中，一定程度的政府干预是不可避免的，德国政府力求尽可能调整所采取的措施，以适应与德国进行贸易的不同国家的需求和贸易条件。

德国经济代表团团长用以下措辞描述了该计划的实际运作情况：

在“新计划”下，德国外贸结构发生了重大变化，主要是在进口方面。进口不得不限制在必不可少的食品和维护德国工业所需的原材料上。同时，由于缺乏外汇，德国减少了从那些因德国出口而产生的购买力不足的国家进口，并增加了从那些能为德国提供市场的国家购买原材料，因为德国没有海外属地可以从中获取所需的原材料。因此，她寻求发展与那些生产原材料且需要工业品进口的国家的贸易关系。

在这种安排下，中国获益良多。中国拥有丰富的原材料，并且完全可以将其销往德国市场。至于制成品，虽然中国现在能够部分满足自身需求，但其需求仍在不断增加。如果得到适当开发，中国不仅可以向德国，也可以向其他主要工业国提供极佳的市场。基普博士指出：

特别值得注意的是，尽管根据“新计划”必须减少德国进口总额，但在此期间，德国从中国的进口增长速度超过了其对华出口的增长速度。

不幸的是，德国经济代表团团长未能完全直接和坦率地告知我们，“德国从中国的进口”是否包括目前被另一强国武力占领的满洲的进口。鉴于前述在中国部分民众中普遍存在的看法，这一遗漏尤为令人遗憾；因为在当前形势下，引用我们要早间同行报纸的话说，“不难理解中国人民对于任何可能妨碍他们通过经济和政治手段寻求补救的努力的发展所抱有的严重关切。”

鉴于这个苦难的世界各地不断传来冲突的谣言，目前的国际前景有些令人不安。为了共同避免已经紧张的战争氛围进一步加剧，德国出于自身利益，应发挥重要且有益的作用。她在很大程度上取决于她如何处理在欧洲和东方的外交问题，这将决定各国之间的和平，进而决定其产品的现有市场以及她必须定期寻求原材料供应的来源。坦白说，经济利益是所有战争的根源，经济与政治永远无法分离。

希望基普博士在有机会时，能向中国公众介绍其国家的基本贸易政策，包括具有准政治性质的问题。因为，总而言之，政治与贸易有关。事实上，自第一次世界大战以来德国在华贸易的显著增长，部分可归因于其治外法权的丧失。在其他条件相同的情况下，中国商人自然更愿意向不享有治外法权的公司下单，因为如果交易出现纠纷，他不必面临在领事法庭解决案件的困难。如果德国贸易使团使其贸易政策从中国人的角度来看足够清晰和令人满意，那么，正如基普博士正确指出的那样：

随着中国自然资源的进一步开发——现任国民政府正成功地将兴趣和精力投入于此——德国可以在中国市场上日益满足其对原材料和矿石的需求。

我们可以补充说，中国也可以日益从德国来源满足其对制成品的需求。

German Trade
Mission Group
Visits Nanking
Study Of Economic

NANKING (Central)—
The German Economic Mission to
the Far East, headed by Dr. Otto
Keip, arrived here this morning
at 7 o'clock from Shanghai.
Shortly after arrival Dr. Keip is-
sued a written statement to the
press which reads:
"Besides studying economic con-
ditions in the countries visited with
a view to informing and advising
German interests at home accord-
ingly, the Mission desires to render
service to trade circles in general
by explaining and interpreting the
present organization of German
foreign trade under the 'New Plan'
of Dr. Schacht, Governor of the
Central Bank of Germany.
"The progressive shrinkage of in-
ternational trade throughout the
world during the past years has
caused governments in all countries
to direct greater attention to foreign
commerce than heretofore; and
this refers particularly to Germany
where the lack of foreign exchange
brought about by reparations and
the resultant burden of external in-
debtedness has unavoidably com-
plicated and impeded the transac-
tion of business with foreign coun-
tries.
"The introduction of exchange
control in Germany was necessary
to assure the stability of the Ger-
man currency against the growing
pressure of external debts; but it
was at the same time the means
of preserving the German economic
system and its purchasing power in
international trade and is through
progressive liquidation of the for-
eign debt, paving the way to a
speedy return to normalcy in for-
eign trade relations.
"Thus Germany, like China, has
economic and financial difficulties
to cope with and is seeking a
solution in the organisation of the
country's resources towards re-
covery and reconstruction and in
the development of friendly rela-
tions in her trade with all nations.
China is an important market for
Germany, and Germany is becoming
a growing consumer of the raw
materials and other products of
China.
"In this way Germany seeks
friendly co-operation with the
countries of Eastern Asia by offer-
ing her industrial capacity in ex-
change for the products of their
fields and natural wealth. To
increase the volume of such ex-
changes in international trade
means to benefit the purchasing
power of the masses and thereby
to contribute to the solution of the
unemployment problem and to
further social welfare and peace."

“德国实行外汇管制是为了确保德国货币免受日益增长的外债压力；但与此同时，这也是维持德国经济体系及其在国际贸易中的购买力的手段，并通过逐步清偿外债，为迅速恢复正常的外贸关系铺平道路。

“通过这种方式，德国寻求与东亚各国友好合作，以其工业能力交换这些国家的田野产品和自然财富。增加此类国际贸易交换量意味着提高大众的购买力，从而有助于解决失业问题，并促进社会福利与和平。”

东京，1月18日电（同盟社）。——率领德国远东贸易使团的特命全权公使奥托·C·基普（Otto C. Kiep）博士今日告知日本外务省当局，他将于明日离开此处前往南京，以“消除中国当局对德意志帝国与‘满洲国’之间拟议贸易协定可能存在的误解”。

这位德国特使补充说，在接触中国当局之前，他将首先与其国家驻中国的外交代表进行磋商。

1月10日，“满洲国”外交代表将一项源自日本方面的计划提交长春当局批准，该计划旨在调整目前陷入瘫痪的“满洲国”与德意志帝国之间的贸易关系。

这项在与德国使团协商后起草的拟议协定规定，新帝国每年购买价值3,000万日元的德国机械，以换取德国进口价值1亿日元的满洲大豆。

该使团于去年10月30日抵达日本，在日本停留至12月，随后在“满洲国”进行了为期约20天的考察。

回到东京后，该团成员除了讨论可能的德意志帝国-“满洲国”协定外，还与日本官员就两国间的商业关系进行了磋商。

日本官员抱怨称，自纳粹政权上台以来，德意志帝国实施的严格限制已使两国贸易从有利于德国的1:4比例，转变为日本从德国的购买量是其向德国销售量的五到六倍的局面。

January 11, 1936 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW 187
Germany to Be First to Recognize Puppet State
of Manchukuo?

GERMANY is preparing to recognize the puppet state of Manchukuo! There is no other conclusion to be drawn from the intensive investigations and negotiations extending over many weeks which a German economic mission has been making and which are now reaching a conclusion in Tokyo. Unlike the American and British missions which centered their interest in China, the German mission, headed by Dr. Otto Keip, has spent nearly all of its time in Japan and Manchukuo. Now the members are back in Tokyo putting the finishing touches on what Japanese diplomats call a “trade agreement.” But it is more or less obvious there can be no trade agreement without diplomatic recognition.

The Japanese Rengo service announced in the course of a long report from Hsinking on Dec. 27 that prospects for an early German-Manchukuo trade agreement had been materially advanced by the visit of the German mission. The German experts spent a month in the puppet state and were accompanied back to Tokyo by three high Japanese officials who occupy executive positions in the Manchukuo government. They were Mr. Matsushima, Chief of the Agricultural Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Industry; Mr. Kato, Chief of the trade affairs section of the Hsinking Foreign Office; and Mr. Ito, head of the document section of the Foreign Office. Dr. Keip, head of the mission, was optimistic for the future of Germany’s trade with the puppet state and said that a trade agreement was necessary because of Germany’s extensive purchase of soya beans. But there are rumors that there is more than soya beans behind the German-Japanese negotiations and that the German experts are being consulted on the establishment of certain industries in Manchukuo which Japan requires in her expected war with the Soviet Union. It was rumored, particularly in North China, that the new community of interest which has developed between Japan and Germany due to their mutual hatred of the Russian Reds may shortly develop into an outright military alliance. At present, however, interest is centered in an adjustment of the triangular trade of Germany, Japan and Manchukuo.

The prospects in this regard are considered favorable because Germany buys large quantities of soya beans in Manchukuo, but up to the present, has sold little in the puppet state. On the other hand, Japan buys extensively of German machinery, but sells comparatively little in Germany.

The Nichi Nichi Shimbun, leading Tokyo daily, said on Dec. 12 that the economic mission which the German Government had sent to the Far East was expected shortly to complete the final negotiations for adjusting the trade relations of Japan, Manchukuo and Germany. This adjustment had become necessary, in the opinion of a spokesman of the Tokyo Foreign Office, because Germany, more than any other European country, had felt the force of Japanese competition in Far Eastern markets. The Germans had about reached the conclusion that the sale of their newly-patented machinery in the Island Empire was only serving to increase the competitive strength of the Japanese. Also it was found impossible to adjust German-Japanese trade on the “quota” or “barter” bases because of Japan’s inability to supply the raw products which Germany required and most of which she obtained from Manchukuo and China. The Nichi Nichi stated that while the mission was in Dairen there had been extensive discussion with the executives of the South Manchuria Railway for the sale of German machinery and products of engineering technique. Also it was reported in other quarters that the Germans had held conversations with the directors of the “Kochu Company”, a Yen 10,000,000 concern which the Japanese are now organizing for the exploitation of their new territorial acquisitions in North China.

The Kochu, or North China Development Company, was promoted by Shinji Soko, a former director of the South Manchuria Railway, with the object that it should occupy the vanguard position in exploiting the resources of North China. The capital of the new concern was supplied by the S.M.R. (one-third), Manchukuo Government (one-third) and the balance by the large Japanese concerns such as Mitsui, Mitsubishi, etc. Among the directors are Haruichi Utsumi, Chief of the East Asia section of the S.M.R.; Shinji Okumura, Chief of the business section of the S.M.R., Keizo Ichida, managing director of Yamashita Kisen Kaisha; Kiyoshuke Kotani, S.M.R. Economic Institute; Katsunosuke Shimada, director of Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; Momotaro Miyakegawa, Chairman of the board of Mitsubishi Trading Company; Taro Komosi, director of the Industrial Bank of Japan and also representative of other financial interests in Tokyo; Jun Kawada, director of Sumitomo Goshi Kaisha; and Shozo Murata, president of Osaka Shosen Kaisha, representative of financial interests in Tokyo. According to the Asahi Shimbun (Dec. 15), the formation of the new company was inspired by the War and Foreign Offices of the Japanese Government, the purpose being to “guide” the people in connection with Japan’s exploitation of the resources of North China.

The activities of the German Economic Mission in Japan and early prospects of a German-Manchukuo trade agreement with German recognition of Manchukuo constitute the first tangible evidence of a rapid drift toward a Japan-German military alliance. Recently all of Japan’s military attaches and observers in Europe held a secret conference in Berlin, the purpose being, according to reports published in the United States, to devise means of combatting the “Third International,” another way of stating the fundamental objective—an alliance against the Soviet Union.

1936年1月11日 《密勒氏评论报》 第187页
德国将成为第一个承认傀儡政权满洲国的国家？

德国正准备承认傀儡政权满洲国！从德国经济使团持续数周并在东京即将得出结论的密集调查和谈判中，只能得出这一结论。与将兴趣集中在中国的英美使团不同，由奥托·基普（Otto Keip）博士率领的德国使团几乎将所有时间都花在了日本和满洲国。现在成员们回到东京，对日本外交官称为“贸易协定”的文件进行最后的润色。但显而易见的是，没有外交承认就不可能有贸易协定。

日本联合通讯社（Rengo service）在12月27日从新京发出的一份长篇报告中宣布，德国使团的访问大大推进了德满早期贸易协定的前景。德国专家在这个傀儡国家度过了一个月，并由三名在满洲国政府担任行政职务的日本高级官员陪同返回东京。他们是：工业省农务局局长松岛先生；新京外务省贸易事务科科长加藤先生；以及外务省文书科科长伊藤先生。使团团长基普博士对德国与该傀儡国家的贸易前景持乐观态度，并表示由于德国大量购买大豆，签订贸易协定是必要的。但有传言称，德日谈判的背后不仅仅是大豆，日本正就建立某些工业事宜咨询德国专家，这些工业是日本在预期与苏联的战争中所需要的。特别是在华北地区有传言称，由于对俄国赤色分子的共同仇恨，日本和德国之间发展出的新利益共同体可能很快就会发展为公开的军事联盟。然而，目前的兴趣集中在调整德国、日本和满洲国的三方贸易上。

这方面的前景被认为是有利的，因为德国在满洲国购买大量大豆，但迄今为止在该傀儡国家销售甚少。另一方面，日本大量购买德国机械，但在德国的销售相对较少。

东京主要日报《日日新闻》于12月12日称，德国政府派往远东的经济使团预计不久将完成调整日、满、德贸易关系的最终谈判。东京外务省发言人认为，这种调整已成为必要，因为在远东市场上，德国比任何其他欧洲国家都更深刻地感受到了日本竞争的压力。德国人几乎已得出结论，将其新获得专利的机械出售给这个岛国只会增强日本的竞争力。此外，人们发现由于日本无法提供德国所需的原材料（其中大部分来自满洲国和中国），因此不可能在“配额”或“易货”基础上调整德日贸易。《日日新闻》称，当使团在大连时，曾与南满洲铁道株式会社的高管就出售德国机械和工程技术产品进行了广泛讨论。另有消息来源报道，德国人曾与“华中公司”的董事们举行会谈，这是一家资本为1,000万日元的公司，日本人目前正在组建该公司以开发其在华北的新领土 acquisitions。

华中公司，即华北开发公司，由前南满洲铁道株式会社理事曾根俊夫（Shinji Soko，音译）发起，目的是使其在开发华北资源方面占据先锋地位。新公司的资本由南满洲铁道株式会社（三分之一）、满洲国政府（三分之一）提供，其余部分由三井、三菱等大型日本企业提供。董事包括：南满洲铁道株式会社东亚课课长内海晴一（Haruichi Utsumi，音译）；南满洲铁道株式会社营业课课长奥村信治（Shinji Okumura，音译）；山下汽船株式会社常务董事市田庆三（Keizo Ichida，音译）；南满洲铁道株式会社经济调查所小谷清助（Kiyoshuke Kotani，音译）；三井合名会社董事岛田胜之助（Katsunosuke Shimada，音译）；三菱商事株式会社董事会主席三宅川百太郎（Momotaro Miyakegawa，音译）；日本兴业银行董事小茂志太郎（Taro Komosi，音译），同时也是东京其他金融利益的代表；住友合资会社董事川田纯（Jun Kawada，音译）；大阪商船株式会社总裁村田庄三（Shozo Murata，音译），代表东京的金融利益。据《朝日新闻》（12月15日）报道，新公司的成立是由日本政府陆军省和外务省推动的，目的是在涉及日本开发华北资源的问题上“引导”民众。

德国经济使团在日本的活动以及德满贸易协定和德国承认满洲国的早期前景，构成了迅速滑向日德军事联盟的第一个有形证据。最近，日本驻欧洲的所有武官和观察员在柏林举行了一次秘密会议，据美国发表的报道，其目的是 devise 对抗“第三国际”的手段，这是表述其根本目标——反苏联盟——的另一种方式。

东京，1月18日电（同盟社）。——率领德国远东贸易使团的特命全权公使奥托·C·基普（Otto C. Kiep）博士今日告知日本外务省当局，他将于明日离开此处前往南京，以“消除中国当局对德意志帝国与‘满洲国’之间拟议贸易协定可能存在的误解”。
这位德国特使补充说，在接触中国当局之前，他将首先与其国家驻中国的外交代表进行磋商。
1月10日，“满洲国”外交代表将一项源自日本方面的计划提交长春当局批准，该计划旨在调整目前陷入瘫痪的“满洲国”与德意志帝国之间的贸易关系。
这项在与德国使团协商后起草的拟议协定规定，新帝国每年购买价值3,000万日元的德国机械，以换取德国进口价值1亿日元的满洲大豆。
该使团于去年10月30日抵达日本，在日本停留至12月，随后在“满洲国”进行了为期约20天的考察。
回到东京后，该团成员除了讨论可能的德意志帝国-“满洲国”协定外，还与日本官员就两国间的商业关系进行了磋商。
日本官员抱怨称，自纳粹政权上台以来，德意志帝国实施的严格限制已使两国贸易从有利于德国的1.4比例，转变为日本从德国的购买量是其向德国销售量的五到六倍的局面。
前德国驻东京大使馆商务参赞、现任德国外交部远东商务处处长的卡尔·克诺尔（Karl Knoll）博士正在协助基普博士。

Reich Economic Group

Negotiations To Aid Trade
Scheduled In Berlin

CHANGCHUN, Dec. 9.—(Rengo).
—Members of the Reich Economic
mission to the Far East left here
today after a five-day visit during
which they conferred with "Man-
chukuo" officials on means to re-
vive the moribund German-Man-
churian trade.

While no agreement was reached
for an exchange of Manchurian
produce for German machinery,
officials here indicated that formal
negotiations to that end would be
undertaken after the mission re-
turns to Berlin and completes its
report.

Bean shipments to the Reich fell
off drastically last year as Ger-
many moved to curtail her foreign
purchases. This, mission officials
are said to have admitted, virtual-
ly paralyzed the Reich's bean-oil
industry and caused a slump in

the live stock market and a de-
crease in agricultural production.

feed and fertilizer.

GERMAN MISSION TO

Hope to Establish Reciprocal

BOUNDARY INCIDENT ON
AMUR RIVER

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Hsinking, Dec. 1.
The visit of the newly appointed
German Consul in Mukden, Mr. G. F.
Rosen, to the Capital, has attracted
very wide attention and his visits to
the Headquarters of the Kwantung
Army and the Foreign Department of
the Manchokuo Government are des-
cribed as courtesy visits.
The German Economic Mission is
due here to-morrow and will stay for
three days, during which they will
visit many of the Government offices
and will probably have the honour
of an audience with the Emperor.
They should be able to see for them-
selves that the State is an inde-
pendent one, having a complete gov-
ernment apparatus, equal to that of
any other country, and run on the
most approved modern methods, the
whole of the work being for the
benefit of the people and develop-
ment of the country.

Proposal to Build Elevators

The German Economic Mission
tentatively is planning to establish
bean elevators in various parts of the
country where the largest quantity of
beans are raised, these to be built
with German and Manchoukuo capital,
the special object being to
open up direct transactions be-
tween the Reich and Man-
choukuo. The idea is that Germany
should supply machinery and rolling
stock in return for beans, the business
to be conducted through the Deutsch-
Asiatische Company in Harbin, which
is closely connected with large ma-
chinery and rolling stock manu-
facturers in Germany. Though Ger-
many consumes approximately 1,000-
000 tons of soya beans annually,
these are bought through London and
the Reich has no direct transactions
with Manchoukuo. This fact places
Germany in an extremely dis-
advantageous position, and in order
to ameliorate conditions the Mission
will suggest that direct reciprocal
trade should be established between
the two countries. As the Manchou-
kuo authorities consider the sale of
German machinery would have an
important bearing upon the Japan-
Manchoukuo bloc, the forthcoming
negotiations will be watched with
great interest.

阿穆尔河边境事件

本报特约记者

新京，12月1日。
新任德国驻沈阳领事 G. F. 罗森（G. F. Rosen）先生访问首都，引起了广泛关注，他对关东军司令部和满洲国外交部的访问被描述为礼节性拜访。
德国经济使团预计明日抵达，并将停留三天，在此期间他们将访问许多政府机构，并可能荣幸地获得皇帝陛下的接见。
他们应该能够亲眼看到，这是一个独立的国家，拥有与其他任何国家相当的完整政府机构，并按照最先进的现代方法运行，所有工作都是为了人民的利益和国家的发展。

建造筒仓的提议

德国经济使团初步计划在该国大豆产量最大的各个地区建立大豆筒仓，这些筒仓将由德国和满洲国资本共同建造，其特殊目的是开辟帝国与满洲国之间的直接交易。其构想是德国提供机械和铁路车辆以换取大豆，业务将通过哈尔滨的德华洋行（Deutsch-Asiatische Company）进行，该行与德国大型机械和铁路车辆制造商有着密切联系。尽管德国每年消耗约100万吨大豆，但这些大豆是通过伦敦购买的，帝国与满洲国之间没有直接交易。这一事实使德国处于极其不利的地位，为了改善状况，使团将建议两国之间建立直接的互惠贸易。由于满洲国当局认为德国机械的销售将对日满集团产生重要影响，即将到来的谈判将受到极大关注。

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Harbin, Nov. 26.
The arrival of the German Economic Mission eagerly is being awaited here, as it is hoped that this will lead to much more business being done between Manchoukuo and Germany. The Manchoukuo press also acclaim the appointment of Mr. Rosen, First Secretary of the German Embassy at Peiping, as consul at Mukden. They consider that he is a man of energy and one who will much assist in the development of trade between the two countries. Rumours are current that the Mission intend to discuss the question of Messrs. I. I. Tschurin & Co. which is owned by the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, and has now entered the bean export trade. The proposal is to form a Company with a capital of Y. 5,000,000, half of which is to be British and half German, but the difficulty which stands in the way of such a scheme at present is, that the bank wants cash payment for the properties owned by the company and these are valued at Y. 2,500,00.

Keen interest is shown in German circles in Shanghai over
the mission of Sir Frederick Leith Ross, English economic expert,
with which a parallel is drawn to the German economic mission of
Dr KIEP, expected to arrive in China shortly. German circles have
with
it that the sending of the mission of Dr Kiep was decided upon at
the consent if not at the invitation of the British Government, in
order to study on the spot the possibility of an economic, and
perhaps even political, cooperation in China between Great Britain,
Germany and Japan. With this object, Dr Kiep, Minister plenipoten-
tiary, former Reich Consul-General at New York and Mr STREWE,
respectively president and secretary of the Mission, are said to
be coming to China direct for the purpose of conferring with Sir
Frederick Leith Ross, while the remainder of the group which
comprises Dr ROSENBRUCH, representing the Reichsbank, Dr Knoll,
former commercial representative at Mukden and M. RADEMACHER,
representing the Reich state railways, may first of all go to
Japan and Manchukuo. Dr Kiep and Mr Strewe would thus be entrusted
with the political side of the mission, while the other members
would confine themselves exclusively to financial and commercial
questions. Let us note, here, that Mr Strewe spent ten years in
China before the War. An engineer by profession, he was President
of the German Engineers' Union in China and Editor in Shanghai
until 1916 of the German newspapers OSTASIATISCHER LLOYD (Far
Eastern Lloyd) and DEUTSCHE ZEITUNG fuer CHINA. Moreover, Mr Strewe
and Mr Rademacher formed part of the German Industrial Mission
which came to China in 1931.

The mission of Dr Kiep is to leave Germany on October 12.

A certain number of members of the German Economic Mission
which is going to Japan and China, and which is directed by Dr
Kiep and Dr KNOLL, Chief of the Economic Bureau of the Far Eastern
Section of the Reich Ministry Of Foreign Affairs, arrived at Tokio
via the U.S.S.R. on October 30.

Mr Strewe and Mr Rademacher are aboard the s.s. Scharnhorst
and are expected to arrive in Shanghai November 7. Contrarily to the
page_data.zh:
上海德国界对英国经济专家弗雷德里克·利思·罗斯（Frederick Leith Ross）爵士的使命表现出浓厚兴趣，并将其与预计不久将抵达中国的克莱普（KIEP）博士的德国经济使团相提并论。德国界人士认为，派遣克莱普博士使团是在英国政府的同意甚至邀请下决定的，目的是就地研究英国、德国和日本在中国进行经济乃至政治合作的可能性。为此，据说特命全权公使、前帝国驻纽约总领事克莱普博士和使团主席兼秘书施特雷韦（STREWE）先生将直接来华，目的是与弗雷德里克·利思·罗斯爵士会谈，而包括代表帝国银行的罗森布鲁赫（ROSENBRUCH）博士、前驻沈阳商务代表克诺尔（Knoll）博士以及代表帝国国家铁路的拉德马赫（RADEMACHER）先生在内的其余成员，可能会先前往日本和满洲国。因此，克莱普博士和施特雷韦先生将被委以使团的政治方面任务，而其他成员则专门局限于金融和商业问题。在此值得注意的是，施特雷韦先生在战前曾在中国度过十年。他是一名工程师出身，曾任在华德国工程师联合会主席，并于1916年前在上海担任德文报纸《远东劳埃德报》（OSTASIATISCHER LLOYD）和《德中日报》（DEUTSCHE ZEITUNG fuer CHINA）的主编。此外，施特雷韦先生和拉德马赫先生曾是1931年来华的德国工业使团的成员。

克莱普博士使团将于10月12日离开德国。

由克莱普博士和帝国外交部远东司经济局局长克诺尔（KNOLL）博士率领的赴日本和中国的德国经济使团的部分成员，已于10月30日经苏联抵达东京。

施特雷韦先生和拉德马赫先生在“沙恩霍斯特”号（s.s. Scharnhorst）轮船上，预计于11月7日抵达上海。与此相反的是

that the German Mission will come "in corpore" to visit China.
----------
The German Economic Mission which has been in Japan since Oct.30
last left Tokio on November 27 for Manchukuo. It is understood that
during the pourparlers in the Nippon capital the chief matter of
interest discussed was the increase of Japanese products purchased
by Germany. At the moment the commercial balance between the two
countries in in favour of Germany by reason of the restrictions and
quotas imposed by the Reich on Japanese goods - this to the extent
of six to one. On the eve of their departure for Dairen (26/11), Dr
Kiep, Head of the Mission, and his Deputy Dr Knoll, had a
prolonged interview with Mr MATSUOKA, Director of the South Manchurian
Railway Company. After a tour of observation in Manchuria, the German
Economic Mission is to visit China. It should be noted that the
Mission has been increased by two members : Mr ROSENBRUCH, Reichsbank
Counsellor and Mr STREWE, who passed through Shanghai Nov.7 on board
the s.s. Scharnhorst, bound for Japan.
--------
The German Economic Mission which since November has been in
Japan, arrived at Changchun coming from Tokio on December 4.
After a number of interviews which lasted five days, with the Govt.
of Manchukuo, on the subject of the development of commercial
relations between the new State and the Reich, the Mission left
Changchun on Dec.9th for Harbin. Although nothing official has been
divulged regarding the negotiations conducted by the German Mission
in the Manchukuo capital, RENGO made known in a telegram dated the 6th
that it was a question of the conclusion of a tripartite commercial
agreement between Germany, Manchukuo and Japan. On Dec. 9th, however,
the same Agency reported that the objects and results of the German
Economic Mission to Manchukuo and Japan would not be known complete-
ly until after its return to Berlin.
--------
Two members of the German Economic Mission now in Manchuria,
Dr STREWE, Engineer, and Mr RADEMACHER, Deputy of the Reich Ministry
of Commerce, arrived at Nanking on December 4.
Accompanied by Dr M.M. FISCHER, counsellor of the German
Embassy, they visited the same day Mr HSU MO, Vice Minister of
Foreign Affairs and Mr T.T. LI, Chief of the Waichiaopou Press
Bureau.

自10月30日起一直在日本的德国经济使团于11月27日离开东京前往满洲国。据悉，在日本首都的会谈中，讨论的主要感兴趣事项是增加德国购买的日本产品。目前，由于帝国对日本商品实施的限制和配额，两国之间的贸易顺差有利于德国，比例高达六比一。在启程前往大连前夕（11月26日），使团团长克莱普博士及其副手克诺尔博士与南满洲铁道株式会社总裁松冈（MATSUOKA）先生进行了长时间的面谈。在满洲视察之后，德国经济使团将访问中国。值得注意的是，使团增加了两名成员：帝国银行顾问罗森布鲁赫（ROSENBRUCH）先生和施特雷韦（STREWE）先生，后者于11月7日乘坐“沙恩霍斯特”号轮船途经上海，前往日本。
--------
自11月以来一直在日本的德国经济使团于12月4日从东京抵达长春。
在与满洲国政府就新国家与帝国之间发展商业关系的问题进行了为期五天的多次会谈后，使团于12月9日离开长春前往哈尔滨。虽然关于德国使团在满洲国首都进行的谈判没有任何官方消息透露，但联合通讯社在6日的电报中称，这涉及德国、满洲国和日本之间缔结三方商业协定的问题。然而，12月9日，该通讯社又报道说，德国经济使团赴满洲国和日本的宗旨和结果，直到其返回柏林后才能完全知晓。
--------
目前在满洲的德国经济使团的两名成员，工程师施特雷韦（STREWE）博士和帝国商务部副部长拉德马赫（RADEMACHER）先生，于12月4日抵达南京。
在德国使馆参赞 M.M. 费舍尔（FISCHER）博士的陪同下，他们于同日拜会了外交部次长徐谟先生和外交部新闻局局长李铁铮（T.T. LI）先生。
--------

page_data.en:
THE GERMAN ECONOMIC MISSION.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. D. REGIST. D. 4724A 11 / 12 35）

German circles in Shanghai are displaying great interest in the mission of Sir Frederick Leith-Ross, the British economic expert, which they regard as being similar to the German Economic Mission under Dr. Kiep which is expected in China soon. It is being particularly said in German circles that the dispatch of Dr. Kiep's mission had been decided with the consent, if not at the invitation, of the British Government with the object of studying on the spot the possibility of an economic, even perhaps of a political, co-operation in China between Great Britain, Germany and Japan.

With this object in view, Dr. Kiep, Minister Plenipotentiary who was formerly German Consul-General at New York, the President of the Mission, and Mr. Strewe, the Secretary, are coming direct to China to confer with Sir Leith-Ross, while the rest of the Mission comprising Dr. Rosenbruch, delegate of the Reichsbank, Dr. Knell, formerly German Trade Representative at Mukden, and Mr. Rademacher, delegate of the German State Railways, will first proceed to Japan and Manchukuo. Dr. Kiep and Mr. Strewe will be entrusted with the political phase of the Mission while the other members will deal exclusively with commercial and financial matters.

Mr. Strewe resided in China for about ten years before the war. An engineer by profession, he was formerly the Chairman of the Union of German Engineers in China, and up to 1916 he was the editor of the German newspapers "Ostasiatischer Lloyd" ("Far Eastern Lloyd") and the "Deutsche Zeitung fuer China" ("German Journal of China"). Mr. Strewe and Mr. Rademacher were also members of the German Industrial Mission which came out to China in 1931.

Dr. Kiep's mission is due to leave Germany on October 12. Certain members of the German Economic Mission which is proceeding to Japan and China arrived at Tokyo via Russia on October 30. The Mission is directed by Dr. Kiep and Dr. Knell, Chief of the Economic Bureau of the Far Eastern Section of the German Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

德国经济代表团。
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别分部 登记号 D. 4724A 1935年12月11日）

上海德侨界对英国经济专家弗雷德里克·李滋-罗斯爵士（Sir Frederick Leith-Ross）的出访表现出极大兴趣，他们认为此次出访与即将抵达中国的基普博士（Dr. Kiep）率领的德国经济代表团性质相似。德侨界特别称，派遣基普博士的代表团是经英国政府同意，即便不是应其邀请，旨在实地研究英国、德国和日本在中国进行经济、甚至可能是政治合作的可能性。

出于此目的，该团团长、前驻纽约德国总领事、特命全权公使基普博士，以及秘书斯特雷韦先生（Mr. Strewe），将直接前往中国与李滋-罗斯爵士会谈；而代表团其余成员，包括帝国银行代表罗森布鲁赫博士（Dr. Rosenbruch）、前驻沈阳德国贸易代表克内尔博士（Dr. Knell）以及德国国家铁路代表拉德马赫尔先生（Mr. Rademacher），将先前往日本和满洲国。基普博士和斯特雷韦先生将负责代表团的政治事务，而其他成员则专门处理商业和金融事宜。

斯特雷韦先生在战前曾在中国居住约十年。他是一名工程师，曾任在华德国工程师联合会主席，直至1916年一直担任德文报纸《远东劳埃德报》（"Ostasiatischer Lloyd"）和《中国德文报》（"Deutsche Zeitung fuer China"）的编辑。斯特雷韦先生和拉德马赫尔先生也是1931年来华的德国工业代表团的成员。

基普博士的代表团定于10月12日离开德国。前往日本和中国的德国经济代表团部分成员已于10月30日经俄罗斯抵达东京。该团由基普博士和德国外交部远东司经济局局长克内尔博士领导。

Mr. Strewe and Mr. Rademacher, two other members of the
Mission, are expected in Shanghai on the s.s. Scharnhorst on
November 7. Contrary to the information contained in our last
monthly report, they will not stop at Shanghai but will continue
their journey direct to Japan on the same vessel.

After making a thorough study of economic conditions in
Japan, the German Mission will come to China in a body to make a
tour of inspection.

The German Economic Mission which has been in Japan since
October 30 left Tokyo on November 7 for Manchukuo. The negotiations
undertaken by members of the Mission during their stay in Tokyo
concerned principally the question of increasing Germany's purchases
of Japanese products. At the present time, the balance of trade
between the two countries is in favour of Germany in the ratio of
6 to 1 because of the restrictions and quotas imposed by Germany
on Japanese goods. On the eve of their departure for Dairen on
November 26, Dr. Kiep and Dr. Knoll had a long interview with
Mr. Matsuoka, manager of the South Manchuria Railway.

After making a tour of inspection in Manchukuo, the
Mission will visit China. The Mission has been increased by two
new members: Mr. Rosenbruch and Mr. Strewe who passed through
Shanghai on November 7 on the s.s. Scharnhorst on their way to
Japan.

N.B.: According to the Central News, two members of the
German Economic Mission, Mr. Strewe and Mr. Rademacher, arrived at
Nanking on December 4. Accompanied by Dr. H. M. Fischer,
Counsellor to the German Embassy, they called on Mr. Hsu Mo, Vice
Minister for Foreign Affairs, and Mr. T. T. Li, Chief of the Press
Bureau of the Ministry, on the same day.

在对日本的经济状况进行彻底研究后，德国代表团将集体来华进行视察访问。

自10月30日以来一直在日本的德国经济代表团于11月7日离开东京前往满洲国。代表团成员在东京停留期间进行的谈判主要涉及增加德国购买日本产品的问题。目前，由于德国对日本商品实施限制和配额，两国之间的贸易顺差有利于德国，比例为6比1。在11月26日启程前往大连前夕，基普博士和克诺尔博士（Dr. Knoll）与南满铁路经理松冈先生（Mr. Matsuoka）进行了长时间会晤。

在满洲国视察之后，代表团将访问中国。代表团新增了两名成员：罗森布鲁赫先生和斯特雷韦先生，他们于11月7日乘“沙恩霍斯特”号轮船途经上海前往日本。

注：据中央通讯社消息，德国经济代表团两名成员斯特雷韦先生和拉德马赫尔先生于12月4日抵达南京。同日，在德国大使馆参赞费舍尔博士（Dr. H. M. Fischer）的陪同下，他们会见了外交部次长徐谟先生和部新闻局局长李泰玉（T. T. Li）先生。

page_data.en:
Mission économique allemande

On s'intéresse vivement dans les milieux allemands de Shanghai,
à la mission de Sir Frederic LEITH-ROSS, expert économique anglais,
qu'on met en parallèle avec la mission économique allemande du Dr.
KIEP, attendu sous peu en Chine. On dit notamment dans les milieux
allemands, que l'envoi de la mission du Dr. KIEP a été décidé avec
le consentement sinon à l'invitation du Gouvernement Britannique, en
vue d'étudier sur place la possibilité d'une coopération économique
et peut-être même politique en Chine entre la Grande-Bretagne, l'Alle-
magne et le Japon. Dans ce but, le Dr. KIEP, Ministre plénipoten-
tiaire, ancien Consul Général du Reich à New-York et Mr. STREME,
respectivement président et secrétaire de la Mission, viendraient
directement en Chine pour conférer avec Sir Frederic LEITH-ROSS,
tandis que le reste du groupe comprenant le Dr. ROSENBROCH, repré-
sentant de la Reichsbank, le Dr. KNOLL, ancien représentant commer-
cial allemand à Hankou et M. RADEMACHER, représentant des chemins
de fer d'Etat du Reich, se rendraient d'abord au Japon et au
Mandchoukuo. Le Dr. KIEP et M. STREME seraient ainsi chargés du
côté politique de la Mission, tandis que les autres membres ne s'oc-
cuperaient exclusivement que des questions financières et commer-
ciales. Notons, ici, que M. STREME a fait un séjour d'environ dix
ans en Chine avant la Guerre. Ingénieur de profession, il a été pré-
sident de l'Union des Ingénieurs Allemands en Chine et rédacteur à
Shanghai, jusqu'en 1916, des journaux allemands "Ostasiatischer
Lloyd" (Lloyd d'Extrême-Orient) et "Deutsche Zeitung fuer China"
(Journal allemand de Chine). Mr. STREME et M. RADEMACHER faisaient,
en outre partie de la Mission Industrielle Allemande qui est venue
en Chine en 1931.

La mission du Dr. KIEP doit quitter l'Allemagne, le 12 octobre.

德国经济代表团

上海德侨界对英国经济专家弗雷德里克·李滋-罗斯爵士（Sir Frederic LEITH-ROSS）的出访表现出浓厚兴趣，并将其与不久将抵达中国的基普博士（Dr. KIEP）率领的德国经济代表团相提并论。德侨界特别称，派遣基普博士的代表团是经英国政府同意，即便不是应其邀请，旨在实地研究英国、德国和日本在中国进行经济、甚至可能是政治合作的可能性。为此，基普博士（特命全权公使，前驻纽约德国总领事）和斯特雷梅先生（Mr. STREME）分别作为代表团团长和秘书，将直接前往中国与弗雷德里克·李滋-罗斯爵士会谈；而其余成员，包括帝国银行代表罗森布罗赫博士（Dr. ROSENBROCH）、前驻汉口德国贸易代表克诺尔博士（Dr. KNOLL）以及德国国家铁路代表拉德马赫尔先生（M. RADEMACHER），将先前往日本和满洲国。因此，基普博士和斯特雷梅先生将负责代表团的政治方面，而其他成员则专门处理金融和商业问题。在此指出，斯特雷梅先生在战前曾在中国逗留约十年。作为一名工程师，他曾担任在华德国工程师联合会主席，并直至1916年在上海担任德文报纸《远东劳埃德报》（Lloyd d'Extrême-Orient）和《中国德文报》（Journal allemand de Chine）的编辑。此外，斯特雷梅先生和拉德马赫尔先生还曾是1931年来华的德国工业代表团的成员。

基普博士的代表团定于10月12日离开德国。

Un certain nombre de membres de la Mission Economique Allemande
qui se rend pour études au Japon et en Chine, et qui est dirigée par
le Dr. KIEP, Ministre Plénipotentiaire et le Dr. KNOLL, chef du
Bureau Economique de la section extrême-orientale du Ministère des
Affaires Etrangères du Reich sont arrivés à Tokio, via l'URSS,
le 30 octobre.

MM. STREWE et RADEMACHER, deux autres membres de la Mission,
voyagent à bord du "Scharnhorst" et sont attendus à Shanghai le 7
novembre. Contrairement aux renseignements donnés dans notre der-
nier bulletin mensuel, ils ne s'arrêteront pas à Shanghai, mais
continueront directement leur voyage vers le Japon, à bord du même
vapeur.

Ce n'est qu'après une étude approfondie de la situation éco-
nomique nippone que la mission allemande viendrait "in corpore"
faire une tournée en Chine.

La Mission Economique Allemagne qui se trouvait au Japon de-
puis le 30 octobre dernier, a quitté le 27 novembre Tokio, à desti-
nation du Mandchoukuo. Au cours des pourparlers qu'auraient enta-
més les membres de la Mission durant leur séjour dans la capitale
nipponne, il aurait été principalement question de l'augmentation
des achats allemands de produits japonais. A l'heure actuelle, la
balance commerciale entre les deux pays est en faveur de l'Allemagne
en raison des restrictions et contingentements imposés par le Reich
aux marchandises japonaises et cela dans l'ordre de six à un. A la
veille de leur départ pour Dairen (26/11), le Dr. KIEP, chef de la
Mission et son adjoint, le Dr. KNOLL, chef du Bureau Economique de
la Section Extrême-Orientale du Ministère des Affaires Etrangères

由特命全权公使基普博士（Dr. KIEP）和德国外交部远东司经济局局长克诺尔博士（Dr. KNOLL）领导的、前往日本和中国进行考察的德国经济代表团的部分成员，已于10月30日经苏联抵达东京。

代表团另外两名成员斯特雷韦先生（MM. STREWE）和拉德马赫尔先生（RADEMACHER）乘坐“沙恩霍斯特”号（"Scharnhorst"）旅行，预计于11月7日抵达上海。与我们上一期月度简报中提供的信息相反，他们不会在上海停留，而是将乘坐同一艘轮船继续直接前往日本。

只有在对日本经济形势进行深入研究后，德国代表团才会“集体”来华进行巡视。

自上月30日以来一直在日本的德国经济代表团，已于11月27日离开东京，前往满洲国。据称，代表团成员在访问日本首都期间进行的会谈，主要涉及增加德国购买日本产品的问题。目前，由于德国对日本商品实施限制和配额，两国之间的贸易平衡有利于德国，比例约为六比一。在启程前往大连（11月26日）前夕，代表团团长基普博士及其副手、德国外交部远东司经济局局长克诺尔博士

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, November 13, 1935

Reich Missions
Due In Far East

Two Groups Will Study
Economic Situation
Of Orient

(Reuter's Agency)
BERLIN.—Two German commissions, one official and one private, will leave shortly for the Far East. They will both study economic and commercial conditions. The official commission will also visit all German representatives and chambers of commerce and will examine the possibility of opening up new relations.

The official commission, sent by the Foreign Ministry, will visit Japan, "Manchukuo," China and Siam. It is denied here that it is going to do business or to recognize "Manchukuo," as reported in the Japanese press.

It is composed of Herr O. C. Kiep, Minister Plenipotentiary, former Consul-General in New York, Legation Secretary Dr. Knoll, and Reichsbank Inspector Rosenbruck.

One of its objects will be to explain to German economic bodies the many new laws passed by Herr Hitler during the past three years.

"Just as big industrial enterprises send their specialists from time to time to their clients," Herr Kiep explained the visit at a recent luncheon, "so the German Foreign Office sends its experts from time to time to the representatives abroad."

The Chinese Minister in Berlin, Liu Chung-tseh, has given a luncheon to the Commissions, at which thirty eminent persons from the Foreign Ministry, banking and industrial circles were present. Among them was Herr Kriebel, Consul-General in Shanghai and friend of Adolf Hitler. Herr Kriebel, who is on leave in Germany, was the guest of honor.

Both Chinese and Japanese circles here deny that the Commission will concern itself with recognition of "Manchukuo." "We do not need to say 'til', nor need we recognize 'Manchukuo'," the Chinese Charge d'Affaires said. "By flourishing trade with her already" Manchukuo is thus recognized if not de jure than de facto.

"Germany would not commit such a blunder," commented Mr. Li, Secretary of the Chinese Legation.

The Commission left Germany last night... interest... of the... financial adviser to the Chinese Government.

The second commission will visit China only, and is composed of the Second Group of the German... Herr... Rademacher, director of the German State Railways. They left on October 28 to study conditions.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年11月13日，星期三

德国代表团
即将抵达远东

两个小组将研究
东方经济局势

（路透社）
柏林讯——两个德国委员会，一个官方，一个私人，即将启程前往远东。两者都将研究经济和商业状况。官方委员会还将拜访所有德国代表和商会，并考察建立新关系的可能性。

由外交部派出的官方委员会将访问日本、“满洲国”、中国和暹罗。此处否认该团将如日本媒体报道的那样去经商或承认“满洲国”。

该团由特命全权公使、前驻纽约总领事O. C. 基普先生（Herr O. C. Kiep）、外交部使馆秘书克诺尔博士（Dr. Knoll）和帝国银行视察员罗森布鲁克（Rosenbruck）组成。

其目标之一是向德国经济机构解释希特勒先生在过去三年中颁布的许多新法律。

“正如大型工业企业不时向其客户派遣专家一样，”基普先生在最近的一次午餐会上解释此次访问时说，“德国外交部也不时向其海外代表派遣专家。”

中国驻柏林公使刘崇杰为这两个委员会举行了午餐会，出席者包括来自外交部、银行界和工业界的三十位知名人士。其中包括驻上海总领事、阿道夫·希特勒的朋友克里贝尔先生（Herr Kriebel）。正在德国休假的克里贝尔先生是主宾。

此间的中国和日本圈子均否认该委员会将涉及承认“满洲国”的问题。“我们不需要说‘直到’，也不需要承认‘满洲国’，”中国代办说。“通过与她的繁荣贸易”，满洲国由此得到了事实上的承认，即便不是法律上的承认。

“德国不会犯这样的错误，”中国公使馆秘书李先生评论道。

该委员会昨晚离开德国……兴趣……的……中国政府财政顾问。

第二个委员会将仅访问中国，由德国……第二组……赫……拉德马赫尔先生（Herr... Rademacher），德国国家铁路总监组成。他们于10月28日出发研究情况。

"THE German Economic Mission to the Far East has at 
last arrived at this premier port of China, after its 
visit to various Japanese and Manchurian trade centers and 
North China. The route the mission takes has caused much 
speculation and indeed it. has been suggested from many 
sources that the object the mission has on hand is to con- 
clude certain gigantic deals with certain “foreign” traders 
in Manchuria, especially for the purchase of beans. How- 
ever that may be, the mission was well received in this city 
by the Institute of International Relations. At the recep- 
tion, Dr. O. C. Kiep, head of the mission, delivered an illu- 
minating speech on Sino-German trade relations. 


Dr. Kiep was greatly admired by his audience for his 
simple, direct, and candid manner of expression. The 
shrinkage of international trade through customs barriers, 
quotas, exchange control, and other restrictions, he regard- 
ed as one of the most vital phenomena in the present world- 
wide economic crisis. But the real root of the evil he traced 
to the reduced purchasing power brought about through 
the losses of the World War and the enormous amount of 
debt it left behind. Germany has to bear the brunt of all 
this in the form of crushit:z indemnities, in addition to the 
loss of her former colonies and foreign markets. But 
Germany, under the leadership of the Reichsfuehrer, is 
fighting to deliver herself from the grip of such economic 
crisis. Dr. Schacht, Minister of Economics, has formulated 
the New Plan to reorganize Germany’s foreign trade. Its 
aim is, according to Dr. Kiep; “to rationalize and co-ordinate 
German imports and exports and to prevent a new debt 
arising from an excess of the former.” At this point, Dr. 
Kiep was apologetic and admitted: 

This planned economy has entailed many undesirable 
impediments to the transaction of commercial business to 
and from Germany. But a certain amount of governmental 
interference is unavoidable in every planned economy and 
the German Government seeks as much as possible to 
adjust the measures taken to the requirements and the trade 
conditions of the different countries with which Germany 
is engaged in trade.

man Economic Mission described it in the following terms:

trade, has been subjected to considerable changes, mainly 
on the import side. Imports have had to be restricted to 
indispensable food-stuffs and to the raw materials essential 
for the upkeep of German industry. At the same time 
the lack of foreign exchange has reduced German imports
